Proposes an approach (MicroSkill Architecture: skill capsules + Dynamic Skill Router + guardrail verification + Self-Learning Loop); secondary: evaluates (single case study vs a monolithic-context baseline)
MicroSkill Architecture (authors' own; no version). Baseline: 'Monolithic Context' (all architecture docs, directory structure and foundational source files injected into the context)

Skill capsules in a YAML schema with 5 fields: hierarchical id, domain scope (subset of the file tree), signature (APIs/type contracts), guardrails/constraints (security, coding standards, architectural invariants), canonical boilerplate; a MicroSkills Registry; final prompt = intent + selected capsules + snapshot of files in scope

Developer natural-language intent -> Dynamic Skill Router selects capsules by cosine similarity under a token budget -> agent generates modular additions (Open-Closed: no edits to core) -> binary automated guardrail verification; on rejection, violations fed back and retried -> Self-Learning Loop: quality function above threshold triggers Abstractor Agent to extract and register a new capsule

Model Claude 3.5 Sonnet for both; agent/harness Not stated. Criterion: first-attempt compile + tests pass; violations; tokens. One run per feature, 15 features (Table I).
- Monolithic Context (baseline) + agent n.s. + Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 48,500 tokens/feature; first-attempt success 40%; 12 architectural violations (5 rewrites of core files). Quality does not work; cost does not work
- MicroSkill Architecture + agent n.s. + Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 3,200 tokens/feature (-93.4%); 86.6%; 0 violations; 7 new capsules. Quality works; cost works

Project: one enterprise CMS, 15 feature specifications, within-subjects (same features under both conditions). Configurations: Monolithic Context vs MicroSkill. Baseline: Monolithic Context. Held constant: model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), feature set, system knowledge content. Acceptance tests: 'accompanying test suite' (not described). Repetitions: Not stated (apparently 1). Human intervention: success counted only without manual intervention or re-prompting; otherwise Not stated

MicroSkill better on all metrics: tokens 48,500 -> 3,200 per feature (-93.4%); first-attempt success 40% -> 86.6% (+46.6 points, reported as '+46.6% accuracy increase'); violations 12 -> 0; 7 self-generated capsules (one pattern reused in 4 later features). Significance not tested
Distinguished the two conditions on every metric, but single run, n = 15, no statistics; repeatability not addressed. Limitations stated: single system, domain and model; replication planned

Single system, single domain, single model; generalisation to other domains, languages and models open; cosine-similarity routing may not be optimal (cross-encoders, RL, learned retrieval); scalability of namespace to very large projects and maintenance burden of a large registry. Future: automated capsule authoring via static analysis, fine-tuning for capsule-guided generation, formal-logic guardrails, federated skill registries
